head_meanings: 장황함, 말이 많고 늘어짐(글/말이 불필요하게 길고 지루함)

source: While the Age of the Enlightenment is often heralded as a period of unprecedented progress, there existed a small but vocal contingent of intellectuals and artists who rallied against the unconditional embrace of certain Enlightenment ideals, either during the Enlightenment or in the century that followed. Prominent thinkers such as Friedrich Nietzsche and Fyodor Dostoevsky produced volumes of work deconstructing and cautioning against the endorsement of the universalism and hyper-rationalism championed by other Enlightenment philosophers. In the arts, Francisco Goya, William Blake, and other like-minded Enlightenment-era painters rendered the human individual and the natural world in a state of elevated importance, offering a stark contrast to a Neoclassical school that exalted the Enlightenment as a triumphant re-ushering of Greco-Roman empiricism. The enduring influence of high-profile individuals who opposed certain Enlightenment ideals challenges the prevailing interpretation of the Enlightenment as an unequivocally positive period of change in modern history.
